s1.syndrome_frame: Multiple skin-colored papules on the face and vulva with a gradual increase in number over time
salient_findings: Multiple dome-shaped, skin-colored papules on the face and vulva
Family history of similar facial papules
Histopathology showing buds and cords of basaloid cells with small cystic spaces
key_facts: Patient is a woman in her 60s
Lesions first appeared around 50 years of age
Approximately 60 lesions are present
Lesions are asymptomatic
Medical history includes a meningioma
Family history of similar facial papules in a daughter
No palmar or plantar pits observed
Histopathology of lesions shows basaloid cells with small cystic spaces
Clefting between tumor aggregates and surrounding stroma is evident
Genetic testing revealed a conserved splice-site mutation in the SUFU gene

raw.syndrome_frame: Multiple skin-colored papules on the face and vulva with a gradual increase in number over time
salient_findings: Multiple dome-shaped, skin-colored papules on the face and vulva
Family history of similar facial papules
Histopathology showing buds and cords of basaloid cells with small cystic spaces
key_facts: Patient is a woman in her 60s
Lesions first appeared around 50 years of age
Approximately 60 lesions are present
Lesions are asymptomatic
Medical history includes a meningioma
Family history of similar facial papules in a daughter
No palmar or plantar pits observed
Histopathology of lesions shows basaloid cells with small cystic spaces
Clefting between tumor aggregates and surrounding stroma is evident
Genetic testing revealed a conserved splice-site mutation in the SUFU gene

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of multiple basal cell carcinomas, family history of similar lesions, and genetic testing revealing a mutation in the SUFU gene are all consistent with Gorlin syndrome, also known as nevoid basal cell carcinoma syndrome.

rejected.label: Nevoid basal cell carcinoma syndrome
rejected.why: This is another name for Gorlin syndrome, not a distinct diagnosis

rejected.label: Basal cell nevus syndrome
rejected.why: This is another name for Gorlin syndrome, not a distinct diagnosis

rejected.label: Infundibulocystic basal cell carcinoma
rejected.why: While the histopathology is consistent with this diagnosis, it does not explain the full range of clinical and genetic findings

rejected.label: Familial cylindromatosis
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with cylindromas, not basal cell carcinomas, and is not associated with the same genetic mutation
